name: Plasman - Lawrenceburg Manufacturing
old_description: Plasman’s exterior trim sector specializes in window assemblies and regulators, rack lifts, door frames, and roof rail systems.
about:
Plasman's Lawrenceburg, Tennessee facility operates as part of a global automotive components manufacturer headquartered in Windsor, Canada, with European headquarters in Gothenburg, Sweden. The company traces its roots back over 45 years to a two-person tool shop that grew into a multinational operation spanning nine countries across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The Lawrenceburg site contributes to Plasman's single-source capability covering tooling, injection molding, chroming, paint applications, exterior trim, and assembly. The company runs over 290,000 square feet of dedicated tooling space and employs more than 200 engineers and technicians focused on molding. Its exterior trim sector produces window assemblies, regulators, rack lifts, door frames, and roof rail systems, while additional lines deliver bumpers, fascias, grilles, and subsystem components. Assembly relies on fully automated, complex robotic systems, and surface finishing includes the proprietary Omniluxe® PVD coating and Brilliance paint-over-chrome processes.

Plasman serves automotive OEMs worldwide, providing components that integrate into vehicle exteriors. Its global footprint — with manufacturing, engineering, and sales locations in Canada, the United States, Mexico, Sweden, Norway, Belgium, Czech Republic, Germany, and Japan — allows it to support customers across major automotive markets.

The company emphasizes a collaborative mindset backed by personal commitment and attention to detail, aiming to deliver the right part at the right time. Innovations such as Omniluxe®, an environmentally friendly alternative to traditional chrome plating, and the Brilliance finish reflect its focus on meeting evolving OEM demands and environmental regulations.

name: Plastech Machining & Fab Inc.
old_description: Robotics capabilities helping with our rapid growth in plastics machining.
about:
Plastech Machining & Fab Inc. operates from Bow, New Hampshire, specializing in precision plastics machining and fabrication. The company focuses on engineering-grade plastics such as Ultem, Delrin, ABS, and Acetal, serving clients from prototype through production volumes.

The shop runs 3-axis and 5-axis CNC milling centers, including Hurco VM20i and VMX30Ui machines, Robodrill VMCs with pallet changers, and a 48-by-96-inch Multicam router. Robotics and automation support high-volume work, while a Brown & Sharpe Micro-Hite CMM handles first-piece and in-process inspection. The company also offers engineering prototyping and production manufacturing, with a pathway to transition low-volume machined parts to injection molding through its sister company, PlasTech Molding Solutions.

Plastech serves customers needing tight-tolerance plastic components for complex applications, though specific industry sectors are not detailed in its public materials. Its material expertise covers a range of engineering plastics, and the firm emphasizes shortening supply chains by outsourcing machine work.

Plastech highlights its ISO 9001:2015 registration through TÜV SÜD America as evidence of a rigorous quality management system. The company states that robotics capabilities have driven rapid growth in plastics machining, and it positions itself as a partner that delivers high-quality parts on time while solving complex business problems.

name: Plastic BagMart
about:
Plastic BagMart, based in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, has been family-owned and operated for over three decades. The business began with plastic bags more than 30 years ago and has since expanded its product lines to include paper bags, retail packaging, janitorial supplies, and point-of-sale paper products.

The company operates as a wholesale distributor and retailer, stocking a wide assortment of plastic and paper bags, foam cups, retail packaging, and janitorial items. Orders are typically shipped within 48 hours from its warehouse, with no minimum quantity required—even partial cases are accepted. Local customers receive deliveries via the company’s own trucks, while national shipments go out through FedEx or common carrier.

Plastic BagMart serves individual consumers as well as small and mid-size businesses, including retailers, warehouses, and offices. Quantity discounts are available, and the company also accommodates custom printing requests for bags and packaging.

The family ownership emphasizes personal customer service and a 30-day return policy as key differentiators, aiming to make every transaction convenient whether the buyer walks into the store, orders online, or phones in a request.

name: Plastic Injection Molding | Norco Plastics, Inc.
old_description: Southern California's Premier Injection Molding Company | Large Tonnage Specialists Since 1974
about:
Norco Plastics, Inc. operates from an 88,000-square-foot facility in Chino, California. The company was founded in 1974 by the Williams family in nearby Norco, starting with just two machines. Today, the second generation of the family continues to lead the business, which has grown into one of Southern California's largest custom injection molding operations.

The shop runs 25 injection molding presses with clamping forces from 30 to 2,800 tons, including a 2,800-ton press installed in 2023 that enables production of very large parts. The facility operates 24/7 and employs about 60 people. Beyond molding, Norco provides secondary operations such as insert molding, hot stamping, robotic part removal, and assembly, plus supply-chain services including inventory management and logistics.

The company serves customers across Los Angeles, Riverside, Orange, San Bernardino, and San Diego counties. Its molded components go into construction (weather‑resistant barriers, structural fittings), storage and logistics (impact‑resistant totes and bins), consumer goods (food‑grade, BPA‑free housewares), agriculture (irrigation parts), automotive (tight‑tolerance fittings), and medical (non‑invasive devices, with cleanroom capability available).

Norco emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015‑compliant quality system, backed by a Brown & Sharpe CMM capable of ±0.0001‑inch measurement, and its 50‑year track record as a family‑owned, full‑service partner that can handle projects from prototype through high‑volume runs.

name: Plastics Unlimited
old_description: "A leader in custom thermoforming, composites, & urethane processes with innovations that deliver excellent quality on-time."
about:
Plastics Unlimited operates from a 130,000-square-foot facility in Preston, Iowa. The company was founded in 1993 by Terry, Nancy, and Gene Kieffer on their family farm after the physical toll of livestock farming prompted them to seek a less labor-intensive venture. They purchased a used thermoforming machine at auction, installed it in a machine shed, and began producing thermoformed parts.

Today the manufacturer provides custom thermoforming, composites, and urethane molding, supported by in-house design and tooling, CAD services, and robotic CNC trimming. The facility houses multiple thermoforming machines capable of handling both small and large parts, and the company's proprietary TEC® (Tooless Engineered Composites) process combines plastics and composites to produce Class-A surfaces with reduced tooling. Secondary operations and assembly are also offered.

The company serves agriculture, construction, dunnage, material handling, medical, OEM, outdoor/recreation, aerospace, industrial, and transportation markets. Its agricultural roots give it particular insight into farm equipment components, while its composites and urethane capabilities address medical device housings, construction equipment hoods, and returnable packaging for industrial clients.

The founders chose thermoforming for its lower entry cost compared to injection molding and built the business on farming values—planet stewardship, quality, innovation, a can-do attitude, and customer service. Plastics Unlimited emphasizes green innovation, award-winning quality, and faster turnaround times than alternative plastic processes.

Plastics, Inc. operates from Idaho Falls, Idaho, where it has been in the plastic injection business for nearly 30 years. The company emphasizes that its custom plastic fabrications are produced domestically, with no outsourcing to China.

The shop provides a full range of plastic manufacturing services, including precision injection molding for parts weighing from 0.005 to 9 pounds, plastic welding (including sonic welding), plastic fabrication, CNC machining, thermoforming, prototyping, and assembly. It also offers custom design support using CAD.

The company serves the electronics industry, producing housings and enclosures, and positions itself as a single-source provider for prototyping, manufacturing, and tooling.

Plastics, Inc. differentiates itself by keeping all production in the United States, leveraging over 40 years of combined experience, and offering post-machining, sonic welding, and assembly under one roof.
